key_insight: Platinum photoelectron spectra are shaped by both many-body satellite/loss processes and strong relativistic spin-orbit effects, and the paper builds a unified spectroscopic assignment across core and valence states.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a reliable reference for interpreting Pt spectra in catalysts and 5d materials, improving chemical-state analysis and electronic-structure modeling.
method: Combined RHEELS with soft X-ray and hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy
Assigned satellite and loss features across shallow/deep core levels using spectral correlation
Benchmarked valence spectra against DFT and G0W0 calculations with and without spin-orbit coupling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic experimental spectra plus ab initio comparison, enabling identification of previously unresolved satellite features, spin-orbit splittings, and loss mechanisms.
watch_item: Spectral assignments are material- and measurement-condition dependent, so applying the Pt reference to other systems or setups should account for calibration and final-state effects.
paper_title: Lifetime effects and satellites in the photoelectron spectrum of platinum metal
